items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: Crooke, banjo player formerly with Alphonso Trent.

ctx.x: Certainly I did. He had A.C. Godley (Sensational) Gardley on drums. Alphonso Trent. Crook was his banjo player. He didn't play guitar in that band, he played banjo. Chester Clark, first trumpet player. Oh, yeah, a fellow was

telling me -- Arthur Hines, again, that he used to go -- Crooke finally settled in New York as a super in an apartment building. Say he used to go by and they'd play cards together. Crooke, banjo player formerly with Alphonso Trent. And good banjo player, rhythm-wise. Whatever way he played on the banjo. But it was good.

I wanted to ask you, too, did -- something I forgot to ask you the first time. Like, when the guys weren't working, like, during the day or something, where did they hang out? What kind of places? Were there many musicians' hang-outs that you remember, like in the '30s and '40s, or did you -
